question: Why are dot products scaled by the square root of key dimension d_k in attention?
answer:
Dot products between queries and keys grow large as the key dimension d_k increases, which pushes the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients; scaling by 1/√d_k mitigates this effect. [Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4)]

Because the components of queries and keys have variance 1, the dot product has variance d_k, so dividing by √d_k normalizes the magnitude of the dot products. [Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4)]

The Scaled Dot-Product Attention computes QK^T divided by √d_k before applying softmax, explicitly incorporating the scaling factor. [Attention Is All You Need (arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4)]

question: What is Mimi and how does it tokenize audio using semantic and acoustic information?
answer:
Mimi is a tokenization system that processes audio in 80 ms frames, outputting a latent timestep that can be decoded back to the same 80 ms of audio. [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue (arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 10)]

Mimi uses distillation to transfer non‑causal high‑level semantic information into the tokens generated by a causal model, enabling streaming encoding and decoding of combined semantic‑acoustic tokens. [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue (arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 9)]

Without distillation, Mimi’s semantic tokens have poor phonetic discriminability, but after distilling WavLM they achieve improved linguistic content capture; Mimi operates at about 1.5 kbps bitrate. [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue (arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 24)]

question: How does H-Net learn content-aware chunk boundaries through end-to-end training?
answer:
H‑Net learns chunking boundaries end‑to‑end, enabling it to adaptively identify semantically meaningful units rather than using fixed rules. [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling (arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 6)]

During training H‑Net predominantly places boundaries at whitespace characters, showing it learns that word boundaries serve as natural semantic units. [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling (arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 14)]
